data.name: Anarghya
data.gender_notes: Anarghya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anarghya is a Sanskrit name derived from the root word 'anargha' which means 'freedom from pain, sorrow, or misery'. It is a name of the Goddess Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. The name Anarghya carries the meaning “Freedom from pain, sorrow” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anarghya usually hope their child will grow to embody freedom from pain, sorrow and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the attainment of inner peace and freedom from worldly suffering.
data.etymology: Anarghya belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Freedom from pain, sorrow.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anarghya total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

Anarghya is a name that signifies blessings and good fortune, as it is derived from the name of the goddess Lakshmi. data.spiritual_significance: Anarghya is a name that carries deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. It is a representation of the goddess Lakshmi, who is revered as the embodiment of wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. Lakshmi is also known as the giver of grace, bliss, and protection. The name Anarghya reflects the spiritual belief that with God's grace, one can attain freedom from all forms of suffering and misery in life. It also signifies the pursuit of spiritual wealth, which is believed to be more enduring and valuable than material wealth. The name Anarghya is a reminder to seek inner peace, happiness, and spiritual growth, and to trust in the divine to deliver us from our problems and challenges.

historical_references.reference: Anarghya was a prominent wife of the powerful king Bharata, who ruled Haihayas in the Ikshvaku dynasty around 15th century BCE.
historical_references.context: Anarghya was a significant figure in Hindu mythology, known for her beauty and virtues. She was the wife of Bharata, the king of the Haihayas, who ruled during the Ikshvaku dynasty around the 15th century BCE. There are various stories and legends associated with Anarghya, showcasing her devotion, grace, and strength.

historical_references.reference: Another reference describes Anarghya as a devoted wife of sage Vyasa, who bore him a son Krishna Dwaipayana (Vyasa's other son was the great sage, Vyasa himself). This reference is from Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic written between the 4th and the 3rd century BCE.
historical_references.context: Anarghya is mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata as a devoted wife of the great sage Vyasa, who bore him a son Krishna Dwaipayana. Although Vyasa was already a great sage, he had no offspring of his own, and he longed for a son. Anarghya, a virtuous and selfless woman, offered herself to Vyasa as a wife and bore him a son, who would later be known as Krishna Dwaipayana or Vyasa's son.

On Pinterest, it is used as a search term for artwork, designs, and inspiration related to Contemporary Indian Art and Culture.
